chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who stands in the row behind the Imam, and there is no one on his left. How should he greet? He (peace be upon him) said: He should greet once on his right.
ai.seo_question: How should an Imam or worshipper perform the final greeting (taslim) if he is standing alone behind the main Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuance of the final salutation (taslim) for a solitary worshipper or Imam standing alone in a row, prescribing a single turn to the right when no companion is present on the left. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the completeness of the prayer ritual even in minimal congregational settings, ensuring the greeting fulfills its social and spiritual function of peace. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of fiqh to varying prayer configurations while maintaining ritual integrity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who is standing in the row behind the prayer leader, and there is no one on his left. How should he greet (Salām)?’ Heasws said: ‘He should greet once on his right’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al- Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus’ab who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) behind an Imam and there is no one on his left side; how he says the phrase of offering greeting of peace?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He says the phrase of offering greeting of peace only once to his right side.’”
